approachQuestion.prompt:
Beacon Ledger
Beacon i emits at period[i], 2*period[i], 3*period[i], and so on. Return the first q events as (time,ID), ordered by time then ID; simultaneous events from different beacons are separate. Example: periods=[2,3], q=5 → [(2,0),(3,1),(4,0),(6,0),(6,1)].

1 ≤ n ≤ 100000 beacons; n ≤ q ≤ 200000. IDs are array indices. 1 ≤ period[i] ≤ 1000000000. All event times needed fit signed 64 bits. Periods are read-only. Output is separate. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000 beacons; n ≤ q ≤ 200000. IDs are array indices. 1 ≤ period[i] ≤ 1000000000. All event times needed fit signed 64 bits. Periods are read-only. Output is separate.

options.text: Build a min-heap of (period[i],i). Repeatedly remove the smallest (time,i), append it, and insert (time+period[i],i), until q events are written.
options.feedback: Exactly the next unreported event of each beacon remains eligible. Advancing from that event’s own time preserves the beacon’s schedule even when several beacons tie.

options.text: Keep next times in an unsorted array. For each output scan all n entries for the smallest (time,ID), then advance that beacon.
options.feedback: This gives the same sequence but repeatedly scans all next-event candidates.

options.text: Sort beacons once by period and cycle through that ID order q times, using each beacon’s next emission.
options.feedback: For periods [2,3], after times 2 and 3 the next two are 4 and 6 from ID 0 before ID 1’s time-6 event; a fixed cycle violates the tie order.

options.text: When a beacon fires, schedule its next emission at globalOutputCount+period[i].
options.feedback: Output count is not clock time. For periods [3] after the first event at 3, this schedules 4 instead of 6.

feedback.reason: Exactly the next unreported event of each beacon remains eligible. Advancing from that event’s own time preserves the beacon’s schedule even when several beacons tie.

One pending event per beacon is enough because its next event follows its current one. After emission replace time by time+period. The heap's full (time,ID) ordering resolves simultaneous events deterministically.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A with a bottom-up built binary heap of n entries; use root replacement followed by repair for each of q events. The heap is not copied for output, and every output event record is written once. Let n and q≥n be as above. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + q log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(q log(q+1)) time, O(q) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build n event heads, then perform one heap replacement for each of q outputs.
details: Initial copy and heap construction cost O(n). Every event replaces one root, requiring up to the heap height; simultaneous equal-period beacons can force full-height repairs repeatedly. One pending event per beacon uses O(n) auxiliary space, independent of q. Output writing costs O(q) time; output is excluded from space.
“O(nq) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: That describes scanning every beacon for each event; the heap avoids the scan.
“O(q log(q+1)) time, O(q) auxiliary space”: This is a looser bound that mistakes output count for active heap size; n can be much smaller than q.
“O(n+q) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: For variable n, repairs are not constant-time and n pending records need storage.
